children: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 0.8% to close at 36,270 on Monday, weighed down by losses in the financial and mining sectors.
Renewed tensions in the Middle East fueled inflation concerns, while hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh strengthened expectations for a September rate hike.
Major banks posted losses despite expectations for the BoC to hold rates on Wednesday, with TD Bank down 0.6% and BMO and Scotiabank losing 1.2%.
Lower gold prices pressured miners, with Agnico Eagle falling 1.9%, Barrick losing 2.2% and WPM retreating 2%.
Most tech stocks also declined, tracking losses among US hyperscalers, with Shopify sliding 3.8% and Constellation Software down 0.8%.
In contrast, higher crude prices supported energy producers, with Canadian Natural up 2% and Suncor rising 1.8%.
The TSX gained 1.3% in August, marking a fifth consecutive monthly gain.

title: TSX Falls on Financials and Mining Losses
